case_title: Munnawar and Ors. v. State of U.P. Etc.
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of Section 302, convicted under Section 307
neutral_facts: The accused fired a shot at the victim during an incident that occurred while the victim and his brother were on their way to a court hearing. The victim was seriously injured and taken to a hospital, where he was examined by a doctor. A dying declaration was recorded by an executive magistrate, which detailed the identity of the assailants, the weapon used, and the site of the injury. The victim succumbed to his injuries after five days, with the cause of death attributed to septicemia resulting from the gunshot wound. The prosecution relied on the testimony of the victim's brother and other witnesses, as well as the dying declaration and medical evidence. The trial court acquitted the accused of murder but convicted them under Section 307 for causing grievous harm. The High Court overturned this decision and convicted the accused under Section 302/149 for murder.
